title: Celeste Was Built in Four Days Before It Won at The Game Awards
hook: Celeste began in 2015 as a four day PICO-8 game jam project, then became a Game of the Year nominee that still hides that original version inside it. This week its co-creator's studio revealed its next game, City of None. Have you ever made it to the top of Celeste Mountain?
script: Did you know Celeste, one of the most celebrated indie games of the last decade, was first built in just four days? In the summer of two thousand fifteen, Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry made a tiny platformer for PICO-8, a fantasy console with strict limits. It was a game jam project about climbing a mountain, and they finished it in four days. They spent the next couple of years turning it into a full game with a story, a soundtrack and a much bigger mountain. The finished game launched in late January of two thousand eighteen on Switch, PC, PlayStation Four and Xbox One. The team even recreated the original four day version inside the finished game as a hidden unlockable, tucked away in a secret room. At The Game Awards that December, Celeste was nominated for Game of the Year. It lost that one to God of War, but it took home Best Independent Game and Games for Impact. And this week, at Nintendo's Indie World showcase on October twenty eighth, co creator Noel Berry's studio Extremely OK Games revealed City of None. It is a new action and puzzle platformer coming to Switch Two and Switch in two thousand twenty seven. Have you ever made it to the top of Celeste Mountain? Follow for more gaming history.
